extracted.intended_audience: sports media, broadcasters, team PR staffs, and fans seeking official biographical information on NBA referees
extracted.subtask_description: Concise professional biographies of NBA referees for a media guide or press kit, listing experience, notable assignments, education, community work, and personal details. Entries follow a consistent header + paragraph format summarizing career statistics and background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard header fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin each entry with a compact header including: NBA Experience (years), Currently in his/her Xth NBA season, Born (date and place), Resides, HS, College.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show the exact header order and short labels (e.g., 'NBA Experience: 15 seasons', 'Born: July 15, 1965 (New Orleans)'). Keep headers uniform across entries for quick scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career game counts and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report counts of games officiated (regular season, playoff, Finals), and mention All-Star/Game appearances where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit numbers and categories as shown ('1,242 regular season NBA games and 62 Playoff games', 'including 33 NBA Finals games'). Include totals for regular season, playoffs, Finals, All-Star and other special games.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior officiating experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail prior leagues and levels of officiating (CBA, NBA D-League, WNBA, USBL, collegiate conferences, high school, Pro-Am), with seasons/years when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List notable previous assignments (e.g., 'four years in the CBA', 'worked the 2008 NBA D-League All-Star Game') and specific conference names (Big Ten, ACC, SEC, etc.) to demonstrate breadth of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable assignments and honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Call out distinguished assignments (All-Star Game, Olympic Games, Japan Games, Mexico Challenge), tournament selections, and awards or honors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include event name and year when possible (e.g., 'officiated the 2004 Olympic Games in Athens', 'recipient of the 1998 Monarch Award'). Mention Hall of Fame inductions or organizational awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and athletic background
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the subject's college(s), degrees, and any collegiate/high-school athletic participation or honors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide degree and institution (e.g., 'Bachelor of Arts in Mass Communications, Xavier University'), and note if they were letter winners or received athletic awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community involvement and charitable work
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize community programs, scholarships, charitable affiliations, and outreach activities the official participates in or founded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific programs and their beneficiaries (e.g., 'NBA Read to Achieve programs at two Chicago Public schools', 'created the Kennedy Leigh Kirkland Memorial Scholarship Fund') to show civic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal/background humanizing details
rubrics_metrics.description: Add brief personal information such as hobbies, family, prior non-officiating careers, and places of residence to humanize the profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep to one or two short sentences (e.g., 'enjoys fishing, horseback riding, pool, weight training, bowling and golf', 'worked as a computer programmer before joining the NBA').

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronology and phrasing conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use consistent tense and chronology phrasing: 'has officiated X in Y seasons', 'Prior to joining the NBA...' and 'Entering his/her Nth NBA season' to indicate tenure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the template's cadence to make entries parallel and comparable; include season counts and prior-to-NBA clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference and tournament specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: When listing collegiate experience, specify conference names and notable tournament appearances (NCAA Tournament, conference tournaments, NIT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples routinely name conferences (Big East, Atlantic Sun, Ohio Valley) and tournament roles ('selected to officiate the 2007 NCAA Tournament'), which provides evaluative detail about level of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise paragraph format and verbosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep each biography to a short header plus one-to-three compact paragraphs focusing on career stats, background, honors, and a closing personal sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The media-guide style favors succinctness—numerical career highlights first, then background and community/hobby notes. Avoid lengthy narrative; maintain consistent density and structure across entries.
